task.title: Determining if the ordinary place of residence is in question

step.cmd: Determine from the information on file if one of the following situations applies:

ul.li: The client’s residential address is in the same economic region as the mailing address.
The client normally resides in one economic region, but is attending school or training or is receiving medical treatments in a different region.
The client is living temporarily in a different economic region while receiving maternity benefits, parental benefits, CCB or family caregiver benefits (FCB).
The client normally resides is in one economic region, but works in a different region (e.g. the client works in Alberta, but returns home to Nova Scotia during periods of lay-off).

The client is an American who lives in the United States but regularly commutes to Canada to work:
If the situation cannot be determined from the information on file, go to step 12.
If one of the situations applies, go to Ordinary place of residence not in question . Ordinary place of residence not in question
If none of the situations apply and additional fact-finding is not required, go to Reassigning the issue to Level 2 . Reassigning the issue to Level 2

step.cmd: Determine if the client was reached:

ul.li: If the client was reached, go to step 14.
If the client was not reached and did not reply to the N-10-00-00 letter, go to Reassigning the issue to Level 2 . Reassigning the issue to Level 2

step.cmd: In NWS, add details to the draft SROC created during fact-finding or create a new SROC as follows:

ul.li: Details : Document the fact-finding details according to the National Fact-Finding and Documentation Policy . National Fact-Finding and Documentation Policy
